hero.text: Seven kinds of activity, all free. Each one gives you instructions, marks your answer as soon as you give it, explains why, keeps a score and can be started again. Nothing you type is stored, and no account is needed.

blocks.title: How to get the most from these activities
bullets: Read the lesson first. Practice works best when it follows an explanation.
Answer before you look. Guessing and then reading the explanation teaches more than reading alone.
Read every explanation, including the ones for answers you got right.
Do the activity a second time a few days later. That is when it settles.

blocks.heading: Grammar: multiple choice
intro: Choose the correct form. Each answer is explained, so a wrong choice still teaches you the rule.

blocks.heading: Fill in the blank
intro: Type the missing word. Spelling matters; capital letters do not.

blocks.heading: Sentence ordering
intro: Put the parts of the sentence in the right order using the up and down buttons. This activity works with a keyboard as well as with a mouse or a finger.

blocks.heading: Vocabulary matching
intro: Match each word or term to its meaning. The second activity covers the literary terms most often needed in Literature answers.

blocks.heading: Reading comprehension
intro: Read the passage, then answer the questions. This is the kind of passage and question used in Paper I.

blocks.heading: Literature quiz
intro: Naming the technique correctly is the first step in every good Literature answer. These questions practise exactly that.

blocks.heading: Error correction
intro: Each sentence contains one mistake. Rewrite the whole sentence correctly. These are the errors that appear most often in students' work.

blocks.title: Your privacy
text: These activities run entirely inside your own browser. Your answers and your score are not sent anywhere, are not saved after you close the page, and are not seen by anyone. There is no login and no personal information is collected. See the [Privacy Policy](privacy/).

pages.title: How to Use This Site
pages.description: A short guide to finding lessons, past papers, activities and classes on RCF English, and to using the material well as a student, a teacher or a parent.

hero.text: RCF English holds a great deal of material. This page shows you how it is arranged and how to find what you need quickly.

blocks.heading: How the site is arranged
text: There are four learning sections, one resource centre, one section for teachers, and one for classes.

parts.heading: The four learning sections
text: [O/L English](ol-english/), [O/L Literature](ol-literature/), [General English](practical-english/) and [A/L Literature](al-literature/). Each one has a landing page that explains the subject, and a menu of lessons underneath it.

parts.heading: Past Papers
text: [The Past Papers centre](past-papers/) holds past papers, model papers, marking schemes, revision papers and question banks, with filters for subject, year, paper and type.

parts.heading: Teacher Resources
text: [Teacher Resources](teacher-resources/) holds lesson plans, worksheets, marking guides and support for mixed-ability and remedial teaching.

parts.heading: RCF Online Academy
text: [RCF Online Academy](rcf-classes/) describes the online classes conducted by Rohana Fernando, and how to ask about them on WhatsApp.

items.title: Use the menu
text: Every main section opens a menu of its pages. On a telephone, tap **Menu**, then tap the arrow beside a section to open it.

items.title: Use search
text: [Search](search/) covers everything on the site. Every result tells you whether it is a lesson, a past paper, an activity, a class or a policy.

items.title: Follow the trail
text: Every page shows a trail at the top telling you where you are, and a link back to the section you came from.

items.title: Start with the syllabus page
text: Know the shape of the paper before you revise. It tells you what to spend your time on.

items.title: Learn writing step by step
text: Never begin a writing task by writing. Understand it, study a model, find the structure, then write.

items.title: Practise, then check
text: Do an activity, read every explanation, and repeat it a few days later.

items.title: Lesson plans and worksheets
text: Material you can take into a classroom without rewriting it first.

items.title: Marking and assessment
text: How to mark an answer so the student learns from the mark, not only from the number.

items.title: Learners who need more help
text: Smaller steps, more models, more repetition, and how to organise a mixed-ability class.

items.title: See what is examined
text: The structure of the paper, in plain language, so you know what your child is preparing for.

items.title: See what a good answer looks like
text: Model answers with notes explaining why each one works.

items.title: Help without doing the work
text: Ask your child to explain the structure of a task before they write. Explaining is what fixes learning.

items.q: Do I need to create an account?
a: No. Nothing on RCF English requires an account, a login or a password. The interactive activities run inside your own browser.

items.q: Does the site work on a telephone?
a: Yes. Every page is designed for small screens first, including the timetable, which appears as cards rather than a wide table on a telephone.

items.q: Will it work on a slow connection?
a: It should. The pages are plain files with no heavy libraries, no video and no tracking scripts, so they load quickly even on a weak signal.

items.q: Can I print a lesson?
a: Yes. Use your browser's print command. The menus, buttons and footer are removed automatically so that only the lesson is printed.

items.q: Is everything free?
a: Everything on RCF English is free to read and use. Books and study guides are sold separately through RCF Publications, which is a different website.

pages.title: Frequently Asked Questions
pages.description: Answers to common questions about RCF English: what it covers, who it is for, past papers and copyright, interactive activities, RCF Online Academy and RCF Publications.

hero.text: If your question is not answered here, please [contact us](contact/) and ask.

items.q: What is RCF English?
a: RCF English is an educational platform that brings together English-language learning, literature education, examination support, teacher resources, online classes and links to educational publications in one place.

items.q: Who is it for?
a: School students, O/L and A/L learners, adult English learners, private candidates, schoolteachers, tuition teachers and parents. Particular attention is given to learners who need additional guidance, including those in rural and remote areas.

items.q: Who runs it?
a: RCF English was founded by Rohana Fernando, an experienced English teacher and lecturer. His qualifications and background are set out on the [Academic and Professional Background](about/background/) page.

items.q: Does it cost anything?
a: No. Everything on this website is free to read and use. Books and study guides are sold separately through RCF Publications, which is a different website with its own ordering arrangements.

items.q: Is RCF English connected to any government body?
a: No. RCF English is an independent educational platform. It is not endorsed by, approved by or affiliated with any government department or examination authority, and it makes no claim to be.

items.q: Which subjects are covered?
a: O/L English, O/L English Literature, General English and A/L English Literature, together with past papers, teacher resources and interactive practice.

items.q: Why can I not find a past paper I am looking for?
a: Because RCF English publishes only what it is entitled to publish. A paper appears here if RCF English created it, if the copyright holder has permitted its distribution, if it has been personally approved, or if it can lawfully be linked from the official source. Papers that do not meet one of these tests are not published, even if copies of them exist elsewhere.

items.q: Are the model answers official answers?
a: No. Model answers on this site are written by RCF English to show how an answer can be built and why it works. They are teaching material, not official marking scheme answers, and they are not the only acceptable answers.

items.q: Can I use this material in my classroom?
a: Yes, for teaching. Material created by RCF English may be used and printed for classroom and study purposes with acknowledgement. Please do not republish it as your own or sell it. See the [Terms of Use](terms/).

items.q: Are complete poems, stories and plays reproduced here?
a: No. Copyrighted literary texts are not reproduced in full. RCF English provides summaries, analysis, themes, character notes, questions and model answers, with short quotations where they are needed for study and criticism.

items.q: Do the activities record my answers?
a: No. The activities run entirely inside your browser. Nothing is sent anywhere, nothing is saved once you close the page, and no personal information is collected.

items.q: Do they work on a telephone?
a: Yes. All the activities are designed for touch as well as for a mouse and a keyboard, including the sentence-ordering activity, which uses buttons rather than dragging.

items.q: Can I do an activity more than once?
a: Yes. Every activity has a Start again button, and repeating an activity a few days later is one of the most useful things you can do.

items.q: How do I join a class?
a: Choose a class, contact RCF Online Academy on WhatsApp, and you will be sent the schedule, fee and availability information. Registration is confirmed by the teacher; it is not automatic.

items.q: Why are the days, times and fees not shown on the website?
a: Because they change, and publishing an out-of-date schedule helps nobody. Where a detail has not been settled, the site says so honestly. Ask on WhatsApp and you will be told what currently applies.

items.q: Are the classes online or in a classroom?
a: Classes are conducted mainly online, which allows students in any part of the country to attend.

items.q: What do I need in order to attend?
a: A device with an internet connection, a notebook and a pen. Spoken English classes also need a working microphone.

items.q: What is RCF Publications?
a: RCF Publications is the publishing and bookshop division associated with RCF English. It produces practical educational books, English support materials, literature study guides, grammar resources and examination-revision materials.

items.q: Is it part of this website?
a: Yes. RCF Publications is a section of this website, kept separate from the free material so that paid and free resources are never confused.

items.q: How do I buy a book?
a: Choose the title, then follow the payment instructions on the page. Payment is by bank transfer, and you send the receipt through WhatsApp. No payment is processed on this website and no card details are ever requested.

pages.title: Copyright and Resource Policy
pages.description: How RCF English decides what may be published, how copyrighted material is treated, and how to request the removal of anything published in error.
pages.keywords: copyright policy, resource policy, permission, takedown

hero.text: This page sets out, plainly, what RCF English will and will not publish. It applies to every past paper, worksheet, model answer and literary extract on the site.

blocks.heading: The rule we work by
text: A resource is published on RCF English only if **at least one** of the following is true.
The existence of a copy of a document — in a shared folder, on a messaging group, or anywhere else on the internet — is **not** permission to publish it.
numbered: RCF English created the resource itself.
The copyright holder has given permission for it to be distributed.
Rohana Fernando has personally approved its publication.
It can lawfully be linked — not copied — from the official website that publishes it.

blocks.heading: In practice
do: Lessons, explanations and guidance written by RCF English
Model questions and model answers written by RCF English
Worksheets and revision material created by RCF English
Papers whose copyright holder has given permission
Links to past papers on the official websites that publish them
Short quotations from literary works, for study and criticism, with the author named
dont: Copyrighted past papers copied without permission
Complete copyrighted poems, stories, plays or novels
Complete paid eBooks or books belonging to any publisher
Marking schemes we are not entitled to distribute
Anyone's private files, correspondence or personal data
Material of uncertain origin, on the assumption that it is probably fine

blocks.heading: Literary texts
text: Literature teaching needs the text, but copyright law protects it. RCF English handles this in the following way.
Where a text is out of copyright, longer extracts may be given. Where a text is still in copyright, the study material stands on its own and the student is expected to have the prescribed book.
bullets: Summaries, plot outlines, character notes, themes and analysis are original work written by RCF English and are published freely.
Context questions, essay questions, model answers and revision exercises are written by RCF English.
Quotations are kept short, are used for study and criticism, and always name the author and the work.
Complete copyrighted texts are never reproduced.

blocks.heading: Material created by RCF English
text: Lessons, guidance, model answers, worksheets and activities on this site were written by RCF English unless a different author is named on the page.

Teachers and students may use and print this material for teaching, learning and revision, with acknowledgement. It may not be republished as someone else's work, sold, or included in a commercial product without written permission. Books published by RCF Publications are sold separately and are not covered by this permission.

blocks.title: If you believe something here should not be
text: If you are a copyright owner, or you act for one, and you believe material on this site has been published without the right to do so, please tell us. Material that is the subject of a genuine complaint is taken down while the position is checked — it is not left up while the matter is argued.
Use the [Corrections and Takedown Requests](corrections/) page, which sets out exactly what to include so that the request can be dealt with quickly.

blocks.heading: No official status is claimed
text: RCF English is an independent educational platform. It is not endorsed by, approved by, or affiliated with any government department, examination authority or public institution, and nothing on this site should be read as suggesting otherwise.
Model answers and guidance on this site are teaching material prepared by RCF English. They are not official answers, and no guarantee of any examination result is made or implied.

pages.title: Privacy Policy
pages.description: What RCF English does and does not collect. There are no accounts, no tracking scripts and no advertising cookies. Sponsored listings and bank-transfer payments are explained in full.

hero.text: The short version: this website does not collect anything about you. The longer version is below.

blocks.heading: What this website collects
text: **Nothing.** RCF English is a set of ordinary files served to your browser. It has no accounts, no login, no database and no server-side program that could record a visit.

In particular, this website does not use analytics or tracking scripts, does not use behavioural advertising, does not set advertising cookies or cookies of its own, does not ask for your name, email address or telephone number in order to read anything, and does not build a profile of you.
The site does carry paid educational listings and sells books and resource collections. Neither of those changes the paragraph above, and both are explained in the two sections that follow.

blocks.heading: Sponsored listings
text: Tuition classes and courses run by other people can be advertised on this site as paid listings. Every one of them is clearly marked **Sponsored**, and paid listings are kept in their own section, never mixed into the free lessons or resources.

These listings are plain text and pictures written into the site. They are not served by an advertising network. Nothing about you is sent to an advertiser, no advertising cookie is set, and what you see does not change according to who you are or what you have looked at before.
RCF English does not endorse an advertiser by accepting a listing. Anything you arrange with one is between you and them.

blocks.heading: Buying books, resources and advertising
text: Books, resource collections, advertising and class fees are paid for by bank transfer, arranged directly with RCF. The site shows you the account details and what to write on the transfer; your bank handles the payment, not this website.

**No payment is processed here.** There is no checkout, no payment gateway and no card processing. You will never be asked on this site for a card number, an online-banking password, a PIN, a one-time code or an identity-document number, and you should never enter one anywhere on it.

Because a static website cannot verify a deposit, every payment is checked by a person. You send the receipt through WhatsApp, and what you send in that message reaches RCF through WhatsApp rather than through this site.

blocks.heading: Interactive activities
text: The quizzes and practice activities run entirely inside your own browser. Your answers and your score stay on your device, are not transmitted anywhere, and disappear when you close or reload the page. No one — including RCF English — can see how you answered.

blocks.heading: Forms, WhatsApp and email
text: Because there is no server behind this website, the contact forms cannot send anything. What they do instead is write your message for you and hand it to WhatsApp or to your own email program, where **you** press send.

That means the message travels through WhatsApp or through your email provider, and their own privacy terms apply to it, not ours. Please do not include information in such a message that you would not want to share.
Any message you do send is used only to answer you.

blocks.heading: Hosting and links to other websites
text: This website is published through GitHub Pages. Like any web host, GitHub processes the requests your browser makes in order to deliver the pages, and its own terms govern that processing. RCF English does not receive or keep any of it.

RCF English links to other websites — chiefly official examination sources, where a paper is linked rather than copied. Once you follow such a link you are on a different website, with its own privacy practices. Links that leave this site are marked, and open in a new tab. Some official Sri Lankan government sites are served over plain HTTP rather than HTTPS; where that is so, the link is marked. RCF Publications is not an external link: it is a section of this website.

blocks.heading: Children
text: Much of this material is intended for school students. Since nothing is collected from anybody, nothing is collected from children either. No account can be created, and no personal detail is requested anywhere on the site. Purchases and class registrations are arranged by an adult through WhatsApp and a bank transfer, away from this website.

blocks.heading: Changes and questions
text: If this policy ever changes, the new version replaces this page. If you have a question about privacy, or you would like a message you sent us to be deleted, please write to us through the [Contact](contact/) page.

hero.text: Plain terms for a free educational website. By using RCF English you accept them.

You may not republish RCF English material as your own work, sell it, or include it in a product or service that is sold, without written permission. Books published by RCF Publications are sold separately and are not covered by this permission.

pages.title: Accessibility Statement
pages.description: How RCF English is built to be usable with a keyboard, a screen reader, magnification and a small screen, what has been tested, and how to report a barrier.
pages.keywords: accessibility statement, WCAG, screen reader, keyboard navigation

hero.text: This site is built so that it can be used by people who navigate with a keyboard, who use a screen reader, who need large text, or who are on a small or old device.

blocks.heading: What we aim for
text: RCF English aims to follow the **Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2, level AA** as a standard of good practice. This is a statement of intent and of the work actually done; it is not a certificate, and no formal audit has been carried out.

blocks.heading: What has been built in
bullets: **Semantic HTML** — real headings, lists, tables and landmarks, so assistive technology can describe the page.
**A skip-to-content link** at the top of every page, so keyboard users can pass the menu.

**Full keyboard operation** — every menu, activity and form can be used without a mouse. Menus open with Enter or Space and with the Down arrow, close with Escape, and return focus to the button that opened them.
**A visible focus outline** on every interactive element. It is never removed.
**Colour contrast** that meets the AA ratio for body text, headings and interface text.
**No information carried by colour alone.** A right or wrong answer is shown by a word as well as by a colour.
**Labels on every form field**, and errors described in words beside the field they belong to.
**Reduced-motion support** — if your system asks for less motion, animation and smooth scrolling are switched off.
**Large touch targets** — buttons and links are at least 44 pixels high.
**Alternative text** on images that carry meaning; decorative graphics are hidden from screen readers.
**Tables that become cards** on narrow screens, so the class timetable is readable on a telephone.
**No horizontal scrolling** at any screen width from 320 pixels upwards.

blocks.heading: What has actually been tested
text: Being honest about this matters more than a long list. The following has been checked directly:
bullets: Keyboard operation of the menus, the mobile drawer, the search page, the filters and all ten interactive activities.
Layout at 320, 375, 768, 1024 and large desktop widths, with no horizontal scrolling.
Heading order on every page.
Colour contrast of the text and interface colours against their backgrounds.
That every internal link on the site points at a page that exists — this is checked automatically every time the site is rebuilt.

blocks.title: Known limitations
bullets: The interactive activities need JavaScript. Where JavaScript is unavailable, a message explains this and points to the written lessons instead.
Search and the resource filters also need JavaScript. Without it, the menus and the [How to Use This Site](how-to-use/) page list every section.
The site has not been tested with every combination of screen reader and browser. If you meet a barrier, please tell us — that is more useful than any claim on this page.
